subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated same-command nonzero exec outcomes with identical structured failure facts count as no progress even when their output changes meaningfully?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but choosing safety-biased blocking over progress-sensitive nonzero output changes is an availability policy decision that tests cannot settle.

options.title: Accept the safety bias
options.body: Merge after exact-head gates pass, accepting that stable repeated nonzero outcomes are blocked even when their output text changes.

options.title: Preserve semantic error progress
options.body: Narrow the fingerprint to retain selected normalized error semantics, reducing false blocking at the cost of allowing more volatile-output loops to evade detection.

options.title: Pause the behavior change
options.body: Keep the existing output-sensitive behavior until an owner defines a more precise progress contract for nonzero exec retries.

recommendation.title: Accept the safety bias
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head gates pass, accepting that stable repeated nonzero outcomes are blocked even when their output text changes.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the foreground exec contract and are the strongest available routing candidate for the remaining runtime-policy choice.
